operations.value:
Line merging is now built (story WB-01M7ZFJF8JY8JKQZ5HS24RPSDG, on feat/relics): when a task description is edited on both sides of a replay and the edits touch different lines, the replay merges them, stores the result in a description.merge operation, reports it with a description-merged warning, and marks it in show --history. Touching or unmergeable edits stay a description conflict that hands back base, ours and theirs. No conflict markers are ever written, and a merged text is always reported.

What is left to explore here: line merging does almost nothing for the single-paragraph descriptions this project mostly holds, where any two concurrent edits collide on one line. Evaluate sentence and word granularity for those, and what an agent should receive when only part of a merge succeeds. Adopt a finer strategy only if it never writes conflict markers into a commit and never produces text that neither author has seen without saying so.
